subject: chemistry
question_text: What are exothermic and endothermic reactions?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Exothermic reactions
lines: Exothermic reactions release heat as they
take place. For them ΔH is negative.

lines.text: C(s) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g)   ΔH = −393.5 kJ mol⁻¹

steps.why: In an exothermic reaction the products hold less enthalpy than the reactants, and the difference leaves the system as heat.
common_mistakes: Pairing exothermic with a positive ΔH — released heat means ΔH < 0.
steps.memory_tip: Exo, exit: heat goes out, and burning carbon is the standard example.
steps.margin_note: Definition earns the mark; the equation strengthens it.

steps.label: Endothermic reactions
lines: Endothermic reactions absorb heat as they
take place. For them ΔH is positive.

lines.text: Heat released: exothermic. Heat absorbed: endothermic.

steps.why: In an endothermic reaction the products hold more enthalpy than the reactants, and the difference is taken in from the surroundings as heat.
common_mistakes: Giving no example — one standard equation per type completes the answer.
Writing the NO formation value without its plus sign.
steps.memory_tip: Endo, enter: heat comes in. Nitrogen and oxygen combine only when heat is supplied.
steps.margin_note: Box the one-line contrast as the final answer.

insider_note: Definitions alone read as textbook copying. One balanced equation with its signed ΔH value under each definition is what a full-mark answer looks like.
